headline: Violence emerges from resource competition, fear, and grievance—understanding causes helps prevent them
universal_truth: Understanding why something happens is the first step to changing whether it happens
fun_facts: Violence has declined dramatically over human history—per capita, we live in the most peaceful era ever
Most violence isn't between strangers—it's between people who know each other
Economic development and education correlate strongly with reduced violence
discussion_questions: What would reduce violence in the world?
Why do some conflicts turn violent while others don't?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Humans are capable of remarkable kindness—and shocking violence. We build hospitals and drop bombs. We rescue strangers and murder neighbors. Understanding why humans fight isn't glorifying violence; it's the first step to reducing it.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Violence seems irrational, but it often follows patterns. If we can understand what causes violence, can we address those causes before conflict erupts?

options.text: Violence typically emerges from resource scarcity, perceived threat, grievance over injustice, or group identity conflicts—usually when peaceful options seem closed
options.response: Yes. Violence is often a last resort when people feel they have no other options. Addressing the underlying needs—resources, security, justice, recognition—can prevent violent escalation.

options.text: Some people are just violent by nature
options.response: Individual variation exists, but most violence requires situational triggers...

q1.title: Scarcity and Competition
q1.script: When resources are scarce, competition intensifies. Land, water, food, jobs—scarcity creates zero-sum situations where one person's gain is another's loss. Abundance reduces violence by expanding options.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Scarcity and Competition"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Fear and Threat
q2.script: Much violence is preemptive—attacking because you fear being attacked. Arms races and escalation spirals emerge from mutual fear. Reducing perceived threat, even without changing actual threat, can break cycles.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Grievance and Humiliation
q3.script: Injustice breeds violence. People who feel humiliated, disrespected, or treated unfairly are more likely to lash out. Dignity and voice—feeling heard and respected—are violence prevention.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Understanding why something happens is the first step to changing whether it happens. Violence has causes; those causes can be addressed.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 205. Tomorrow, we'll explore stories of what happened—history. Until then, consider what conditions in your environment reduce or increase conflict.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Conflict Conditions - What Triggers Escalation?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify conditions that lead to conflict
growTrack.activity: Think about conflicts in your life that escalated. What conditions contributed—scarcity, fear, grievance, feeling unheard? How might addressing those underlying conditions have prevented escalation? Prevention beats intervention.
